newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba's Gaddum opposes amending EMU pact-magazine.
newsitem.headline: Buba's Gaddum opposes amending EMU pact-magazine.

text.p: Bundesbank vice president Johann Wilhelm Gaddum opposes amending the stability pact designed to ensure fiscal discipline in the euro zone, the German magazine Focus reported on Saturday.
In an advance release of an interview, Focus reported Gaddum as saying he did not see any great leeway to alter to the pact, as has been requested by the new Socialist French government.
Gaddum said the room for compromise had been exhausted on this issue.
European Union countries hope to ratify the stability pact at an EU summit in Amsterdam on Monday and Tuesday.
The Bundesbank vice-president said last week he expected the pact to be ratified in its present form.
The German-inspired pact, which would impose tough sanctions on countries that stray from budgetary discipline once the single currency is launched in 1999, was agreed in Dublin last December.

Abiding by an election pledge to reorient the drive to European monetary union, French Prime Minister Lionel Jospin is demanding that Europe's single currency plans take Europe's 18 million jobless into account.
